name: Fortis Healthcare Ltd.
business_summary: Second/third-largest listed Indian private hospital chain: ~36 facilities and ~4,000 operational beds (screener.in), concentrated in NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Punjab, plus Nepal/Dubai/Sri Lanka, and ~57%-owned SRL diagnostics (415 labs). IHH Healthcare (Malaysia) holds ~31% as promoter. Hospitals ~77% of revenue, diagnostics ~23% (mix = model knowledge). Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026): sales Rs 2,545 cr (+17.5% YoY), EBITDA Rs 537 cr (21%), PAT Rs 273 cr. Targets 25% EBITDA margin by FY28; capex of Rs 252 cr approved (Sahi 2026-08-10). Q2 FY27 results not yet in the pack; due in November (date unverified). Mcap Rs 61,208 cr, P/E 57.

revenue_mix.geography: India ~96% / international (Nepal, Dubai, Sri Lanka) ~4%; model knowledge

exposures.mechanism: SC questioned cancer-drug markups (2026-09-30) and sought a 16% MRP-over-cost cap; the Centre then cut cancer-drug prices ~30% (Livemint/Guardian, Oct 2026) and NPPA is tightening compliance. Pharmacy+consumables ~25% of revenue, of which oncology/high-markup drugs ~5% at 40% margin: one tightening step takes ~1.5% of revenue at ~100% drop-through = -7% EBITDA at 21% OPM; EV/MCap 1.1, persistence 1.0 (structural) but partly passed into procedures -> -5. Stock fell up to ~10% in 2 days (ET 2026-10-01) and recovered partly (+4% on 2026-10-09).

evidence.note: Hospital stocks erase US$2.6 bn as SC questions steep markups (ThePrint 2026-09-30); Fortis -7% intraday (Livemint)

exposures.mechanism: Employee+doctor fees ~40% of costs (model knowledge). +2pp wage inflation = +0.8% of total costs; 50% passed through via tariffs -> +0.4% of costs = 0.32% of revenue (costs ~79% of revenue); / 21% OPM = EBITDA -1.5%; EV/MCap 1.1, persistence 1.0 (wages ratchet) -> -1.7.

evidence.note: Q1 FY27 margin 21% vs 23% in prior quarters; short-term margin pressure (NDTV Profit 2026-08-10)

exposures.mechanism: Elective surgeries, health checks and international patients correlate with urban affluence/insurance penetration. +5pp urban demand -> +2pp revenue; operating leverage 60% incremental margin on ~21% base -> +6% EBITDA; EV/MCap 1.1, persistence 0.5 -> +3.3, haircut for supply-constrained occupancy (occupancy ~70%) -> +2.0.

evidence.note: Q1 FY27 revenue +17.5% YoY on expansion (Investing.com 2026-08-07)

exposures.mechanism: Net debt ~Rs 3,600 cr (interest Rs 320 cr/yr at 8.9%; estimate from interest run-rate Rs 80 cr/qtr). +25bp on floating half = Rs 4.5 cr = 0.4% of EBITDA; main channel is discount-rate on 57x P/E growth stock: duration ~15 yrs -> +25bp = -1.5%; both -> -1.8. Empirical not significant (US 10y positive).

evidence.note: Interest Rs 80 cr in Jun-26 quarter (screener.in)

exposures.mechanism: Direct INR exposure small (international ~4% of revenue; imported equipment largely hedged). Empirical +2.98 (t=2.0, market beta 1.12) is probably FPI/risk-on co-movement rather than a fundamental link. Model: +3% USD/INR -> +0.12% sales from international/medical-tourism receipts, ~+0.5% EBITDA -> +0.5; blended with data shrinkage toward the empirical estimate -> +1.8 (low confidence).

FII holding fell from 26.0% (Mar-26) to 23.2% (Sep-26); stock -20% in 12m, beta 1.1. +US$5bn quarterly FPI inflow -> broad market ~+4%, Fortis beta 1.1 + repositioning -> +2.5 beyond market-wide effect.
Hospital revenue growth ~14-16% organic; +1pp real GDP adds ~0.6pp to volumes -> +0.3% sales... with 60% incremental margin +1.0% EBITDA, persistence 1.0 -> +1.1, sector rerating -> +1.5.
+1pp CPI -> RBI stays higher for longer (rate channel above) and consumables inflation ~ +0.3 pp costs; hospital pricing indexed partly (+3-5% annual tariff hikes) -> net -0.6.

evidence.note: Q1 FY27 earnings call (Yahoo Finance 2026-08-07): tariff and mix drive ARPOB

exposures.mechanism: Mix shift to high-acuity oncology, neuro, transplant and international patients raises ARPOB 5-7%/yr; +1 unit of premiumisation theme -> +1.5.
